purpose: Assigned values for the 8-bit profile_id field as it appears in TRANSPORT_OFFER and TRANSPORT_ACCEPT for the IP binding. Profile identifiers are transport-scoped: profile 1 under IP and profile 1 under BLE are unrelated assignments and must never be compared.

allocation_policy.0x00: Reserved. Never assigned, so an uninitialised field names no profile.

profiles.name: RESERVED
profiles.detail: Permanently reserved. An offer carrying profile_id 0 is malformed.

profiles.name: IP-X0-DATAGRAM-EXPERIMENTAL
profiles.detail: Datagram carriage where the datagram boundary IS the frame boundary: exactly one Link frame per datagram, trailing bytes refused rather than ignored. Rendezvous beacon in a discovery datagram to the provisional unregistered port 49913.
profiles.evidence: mcl-ip/evidence/e4-udp-2g4-20260902/ demonstrated this carriage over 2.4 GHz between two machines, including eight deliberately malformed inputs that were refused. Transport evidence, not a conformance pass: no normative profile exists to conform to.
profiles.promotion_gate: May be proposed for a Standards Action assignment once a second independent implementation has interoperated with it and the parameters are fixed by specification rather than by the reference implementation.

profiles.name: IP-X1-STREAM-EXPERIMENTAL
profiles.detail: Length-prefixed stream carriage with a 2-byte prefix, bounded by the largest legal Link frame so an implausible declared length is refused rather than buffered. Preserves synchronisation across a frame it cannot decode, which is what lets a stream recover instead of resynchronising by luck.
profiles.evidence: Unit-tested only. This profile has not been exercised over a real TCP connection between two machines.
profiles.promotion_gate: As above, and requires over-air evidence first.

notes: Experimental Use values were chosen deliberately over 1 and 2. These profiles are defined by reference-implementation behaviour rather than by specification, and an Experimental assignment says so in the value itself.
The underlying link technology is not part of the profile. Wi-Fi and Ethernet are the same IP profile; the transport identifier names a family, not a radio.
A profile_id says nothing about security. The security_claim field in an IP endpoint is a CLAIM by the offering peer, not a verified property.
An implementation receiving an unassigned profile_id MUST NOT guess. It refuses the offer and may continue on its current transport.
